question.text: A DDQ from an Indian SWF asks: 'Describe your Key-Man Clause and its consequences.' Per Ch 12, the STANDARD investor protection is:

answer.text: Automatic dissolution of the fund within 30 days, with pro-rata distribution at cost.
Suspension of new investments and investors typically request compulsory redemption/exit without charges unless a suitable replacement is found within pre-agreed timelines and informed to SEBI.
The fund must be transferred to an alternate Manager chosen by SEBI.
The Sponsor automatically buys out all LP interests at the last NAV.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Chapter 12, the Key-Man clause prohibits new investments when key persons are unavailable, and investors typically ask for compulsory redemption/exit without charges unless a suitable replacement is found within pre-agreed timelines and informed to SEBI. The Trap: Options A, C and D describe extreme outcomes the workbook does not support - automatic dissolution at cost, a SEBI-chosen replacement manager, or a forced Sponsor buy-out at last NAV. Note: Two source-backed elements travel together: investment suspension on the trigger event, and a redemption/exit right unless a replacement is appointed within agreed timelines and informed to SEBI.
